Multimodal LLM decoding strategies in these papers are mostly inference-time, training-free methods that change which tokens to commit and when, especially for diffusion-based multimodal LLMs. The survey paper groups decoding methods into token-level control, sequence-level generation, and parallel token generation for LLMs and LVLMs [5]. For multimodal diffusion models specifically, proposed strategies include information-guided token ordering with semantic anchors and neighborhood uncertainty [1], visual-complementary parallel selection to reduce redundant grounding [2], context-aware cluster decoding using confidence plus neighbor proximity [3], causal interventions to reduce object hallucination during generation [4], and relevance-based decoding that shifts attention toward perceptual inputs to reduce hallucinations [9].

These methods differ by objective: IGFD and CACD emphasize contextual readiness and semantic anchors [1, 3]; VRCD focuses on avoiding overlapping visual grounding among tokens decoded together [2]; causal decoding and LIME target hallucination resistance and stronger grounding [4, 9]. STDec is related but aims at spatio-temporal stability and speed while maintaining comparable performance, including on multimodal understanding benchmarks [7].
